hypotheses.title: W2-execpolicy: Command policy rules allow/prompt/forbidden with match/not_match examples validated at load
hypotheses.plan: Rules file (ARTEL_HOME/policy.yaml + project override): each rule has a command prefix or regex, a decision allow | prompt | forbidden, a justification, and match / not_match examples that are checked when the policy loads (a rule whose examples fail is an error). bash and the Codex / Claude Code runtimes consult it before running a command: forbidden -> tool error with the justification; prompt -> the task goes to a person (needs_human) with the command; allow -> run. Ship safe defaults (rm -rf /, curl | sh, git push --force on main, credential files).
hypotheses.expected: policy examples validated at load (bad example = load error); forbidden command never executes (test); prompt sends the task to a person with the command; no benchmark regression

hypotheses.title: W2-guardian: Asynchronous trajectory risk reviewer; high risk switches later actions to blocking review
hypotheses.plan: After each worker run, a cheap reviewer (System One or a small model) scores the trajectory's risk from the event log: destructive commands, writes outside the workspace, network exfiltration, secrets in output. Low risk: nothing. High risk: the task's later runs require a blocking review of every shell command by the guardian before execution, and the dashboard shows a risk badge with the reason.
hypotheses.expected: risk score logged for every run (guardian/assessed events); high-risk run switches the task to blocking review; a scripted destructive trajectory is flagged high; cost increase <= 5%

hypotheses.title: W2-fs-grants: Explicit read/write grants per path
hypotheses.plan: Per-role and per-project grants: read paths, write paths (default: workspace + shared deliverables; read-only refs). ToolContext.resolve enforces them for every file tool; the Codex runtime maps them to --add-dir / sandbox, Claude Code to --add-dir and disallowed write tools. A denied access returns a tool error naming the grant.
hypotheses.expected: writes outside granted paths are refused for every runtime (tests); refs stay read-only; grants visible on the project page; no benchmark regression

hypotheses.title: W2-cost-down: Bring cost back down — wave 1 raised the benchmark cost from $4.57 to $5.99 (+31%)
hypotheses.plan: Find where the tokens go (per role, per tool output) with the analytics already logged; then: prompt caching for the native runtime's stable system prefix, trimming repeated context given to reviewer / auditor, cheaper model or lower effort for librarian / refiner / auditor where pass rate holds, skipping roles that add nothing on easy tasks. Each change measured separately.
hypotheses.expected: benchmark cost <= $5.0 with 7/7 passing; no role quality drop on hidden checks
